what_happened: Found that the existing scopes_overlap_first() jq predicate (already spliced into orchestrate-batch-admit.sh via FILE_SCOPE_OVERLAP_JQ_DEFS) can be reused verbatim for the new dirty-worktree-vs-file_scope check by passing the dirty tracked paths as the 'other_scope' argument -- no new jq def needs to be written, matching the established additive-advisory pattern exactly.

test-conflict-predicate.sh and test-four-tier-conflict.sh both run the real orchestrate-batch-admit.sh inside an isolated TMPROOT that is never a real git repository (no 'git init' anywhere in either suite). Exercising the new dirty_scope_advisory's real 'git diff --name-only HEAD' call requires extending both TMPROOT builders with git init + baseline commit + an uncommitted edit, which is a new fixture capability neither suite has today.

Planned file_scope necessarily includes agent-system/extensions/core/context/patterns/batch-orchestration-guardrails.md, which is also in concurrently-planning sibling task 418's declared file_scope this same cycle. Declared it anyway (per batch-orchestration-guardrails.md: shared territory is serialized by the admission gate, never excluded) and carried the hazard into the plan's Risks table plus Phase 5's first task as a re-read-before-edit obligation.

Research report's structural claims were re-derived independently against the source store and every one held (8 whole_tree_claim_frag merge sites, Class J as next free letter, zero git init in either named suite, git-snapshot.sh needing no change). One correction was found and applied: the report flagged orchestrate-batch-results-template.md for doc convergence, but neither later sibling advisory appears there at all, so sibling precedent excludes it. Planning cost was low because the report had already located every anchor.

test-orchestrate-predispatch-review.sh and test-orchestrate-unwind-dispatch.sh fail (11+2 cases) in Phase 1's --only suite run with pre-existing, unmodified failures: their isolated TMPROOT fixture omits lib/project-number-inuse.sh, causing state-write.sh to fail inside the fixture. Confirmed independent of this task's edit by re-running both suites against the pristine (HEAD) orchestrate-batch-admit.sh, which failed identically. Not caused by the dirty_scope_advisory change; left unfixed as out of this task's scope.

Phase 1's manual probe used the live repository as its own fixture: orchestrate-batch-admit.sh itself was the dirty, in-scope file being edited, so running the admission probe for candidate 409 against the real dirty tree exercised the true positive case directly (dirty_scope_advisory fired naming the file) with no synthetic fixture needed; a clean-scope candidate (328) gave the true negative. Saved building a throwaway fixture for this one manual-probe verification step.

test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh fails identically (279 passed, 25 failed) against both the edited and the pristine HEAD copy of orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh, confirming the failures are pre-existing and unrelated to the dirty_scope_ledger addition. test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh itself passed cleanly.
